subject: general
question: Which jurist was designated as the 53rd Chief Justice of India on 30 October 2025 and assumed office on 24 November 2025?
solution:
p>The correct answer is __**Justice Surya Kant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Justice Surya Kant** was officially designated as the **53rd Chief Justice of India (CJI)** on **30 October 2025** and formally assumed office on **24 November 2025**.
 
• He succeeded **Justice B.R. Gavai** (the **52nd CJI**), continuing the established line of succession in the **Supreme Court of India** based on the principle of seniority.
 
• Born in **Hisar, Haryana**, in **1962**, **Justice Surya Kant** has had a distinguished legal career, previously serving as the **Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court** before his elevation to the **Supreme Court** on **24 May 2019**.
 
• His tenure as the **Chief Justice of India** is slated to last until **9 February 2027**, when he will reach the mandatory retirement age of **65 years**.
 
• During his career, he has been part of several landmark judgments involving **constitutional law**, **fundamental rights**, and **administrative reforms**, contributing significantly to Indian jurisprudence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Justice B.V. Nagarathna:** A sitting judge of the **Supreme Court of India**, she is widely recognized for the historic possibility of becoming the **first woman Chief Justice of India**. Her projected tenure as CJI is expected to begin in **September 2027**, though it will be for a relatively short duration of **36 days**.
 
• **Justice P.S. Narasimha:** He was elevated directly from the **Bar** to the **Supreme Court bench** in **August 2021**. He is also in the line of succession to become the **Chief Justice of India** in the **year 2027-28**.
 
• **Justice Vikram Nath:** Formerly the **Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court**, he was among the nine judges appointed to the **Supreme Court** in **2021** and is another key figure in the seniority-based succession for the top judicial post.
 
• **Appointment Process:** Under **Article 124** of the **Constitution of India**, the **President of India** appoints the **Chief Justice**. By convention, the outgoing **CJI** recommends the name of the most senior judge of the **Supreme Court** as their successor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Collegium System:** This is the system by which judges are appointed and transferred in the **Supreme Court** and **High Courts**. It consists of the **Chief Justice of India** and the four most senior judges of the **Supreme Court**.
 
• **Retirement and Qualifications:** A judge of the **Supreme Court** must be a citizen of **India** and must have been a judge of a **High Court** for at least **5 years** or an advocate of a **High Court** for **10 years**. The retirement age is fixed at **65 years**.
 
• **Constitutional Oath:** Every person appointed to be a judge of the **Supreme Court** shall, before entering upon office, make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before the **President of India** according to the form set out in the **Third Schedule** of the **Constitution**.
 
• **Removal:** A judge can only be removed from office by an order of the **President** passed after an address by each **House of Parliament** (supported by a special majority) on the grounds of **proved misbehaviour or incapacity**.
